Calibrate an intensity intervention to a target value

Source: R/calibrate-alpha.R
calibrate_alpha.Rd

Finds the intervention alpha on the intensity of the process z_name such that the estimated risk of z_name (the exposure) equals a calibration target theta, and estimates the risk of each target under that calibrated intervention. The standard errors of the latter account for the estimation of alpha.

Usage

calibrate_alpha(
  initial_fit,
  target,
  z_name,
  value,
  scale = c("absolute", "ratio", "difference"),
  a = NULL,
  reference_a = a,
  estimand = c("risk", "years_lost"),
  exposure_estimand = c("risk", "years_lost"),
  control = list(),
  cores = 1,
  verbose = FALSE
)

Arguments

initial_fit

An initial fit, as returned by fit_initial().

target

Character vector. Names of the processes whose risks are estimated under the calibrated intervention.

z_name

String. Name of the process in initial_fit whose intensity is intervened on and calibrated.

value

Number. The calibration target on the scale, see Description. Must be non-negative unless scale = "difference".

scale

The scale of value: "absolute", "ratio" or "difference", see Description.

a

Optional baseline treatment value (0 or 1) to intervene on, as in tmle_alpha().

reference_a

Optional baseline treatment value (0 or 1) under which the reference exposure of a "ratio" or "difference" scale is estimated. Defaults to a; e.g. a = 1, reference_a = 0 calibrates the exposure under treatment to that under placebo.

estimand

The target parameter for target, as in tmle_alpha().

exposure_estimand

The target parameter for the exposure z_name, that value and the calibration refer to, as in tmle_alpha().

control

Settings for the estimates, passed on to tmle_alpha().

cores

Positive integer. Number of cores used by parallel::mclapply() for the per-individual computations.

verbose

Logical. If TRUE, print progress.

Value

An object of class calibrate_alpha, a list with elements:

  • estimate: a data.table with one row per target and columns target, the risk estimate under the calibrated intervention, its standard error se (accounting for the estimation of alpha), the bounds lower and upper of a 95% Wald confidence interval, and the standard error se_crude treating alpha as known.

  • calibration: a data.table with the calibrated alpha and the calibration target theta (column quantity), with estimate, se, lower and upper.

  • z_name, a, value, scale, reference_a, estimand and exposure_estimand: as given (reference_a is NULL for the "absolute" scale).

  • eic, eic_alpha_known: lists, named by target, of the influence curves of the risk of target, accounting for the estimation of alpha and treating it as known.

  • alpha_eic: the influence curve of the calibrated alpha.

  • checks: diagnostics of the alpha search (converged, dist, c_n) and the estimated derivatives with respect to alpha of the risk of z_name (derivative_z) and of each target (derivative_target).

Details

The calibration target theta is given by value on the scale:

  • "absolute": theta = value.

  • "ratio": theta = value * reference.

  • "difference": theta = value + reference.

where reference is the exposure without intervention on z_name, under the baseline treatment reference_a.

Examples

fit <- fit_initial(
  illness_death,
  fit_types = list(
    z = list(
      delta = 2,
      model = ~ L0,
      at_risk = function(dt) dt[["z"]] == 0
    ),
    death = list(delta = 1, model = ~ L0 + z),
    censoring = list(delta = 0, model = ~ L0)
  ),
  tau = 1
)

# Risk of death under the intervention on z that brings the risk of z
# down to 80% of its observed value.
cal <- calibrate_alpha(
  fit,
  target = "death",
  z_name = "z",
  value = 0.8,
  scale = "ratio"
)
cal$estimate
#>    target  estimate         se     lower     upper   se_crude
#>    <char>     <num>      <num>     <num>     <num>      <num>
#> 1:  death 0.3199203 0.03864198 0.2441835 0.3956572 0.03866085
